title: [CL-1248] Add FAB button component to vault
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

[CL-1248](https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/CL-1248)

## 📔 Objective

Adds a `BitFabComponent` (Floating Action Button) to the component library — a circular primary button for a single high-priority action. Accepts a `BitwardenIcon`, an accessible `label`, and a `disabled` state.

## 📸 StoryBook

[StoryBook!](https://62a88a6de5b807fa98886113-vhcbdydiwf.chromatic.com/?path=/docs/vault-fab--docs)

inline.body:
♻️ **DEBT**: FAB opts into `ButtonLikeAbstraction` but never renders a loading indicator.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

The component provides `ButtonLikeAbstraction` (line 26) and re-exposes `loading`, so `bitAction` / `bitFormButton` resolve against it and call `loading.set(true)` during async work. However `fab.component.html` only renders `<bit-icon>` — there is no spinner branch like `button.component.html` and `icon-button.component.html` have, and `loading` is not forwarded through `hostDirectives` inputs either.

Result: a FAB used with `[bitAction]` goes to the disabled color treatment for the duration of the action with no progress feedback, which diverges from the other button-like components.

Two ways to close the gap:
- Render the spinner when `baseButton.showLoadingStyle()` is true, mirroring `icon-button.component.html`, and forward `loading` in the `BaseButtonDirective` host-directive inputs; or
- Drop the `ButtonLikeAbstraction` provider if loading is intentionally out of scope for v1, so async-action directives can't silently attach.
</details>

❓ **QUESTION**: `package-lock.json` changed without a corresponding `package.json` change — was this intentional?

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

The lock diff is unrelated to the FAB component: new optional/peer entries (`chokidar@4.0.3`, `readdirp@4.1.2`, `utf-8-validate@5.0.10`) plus ~40 packages reclassified from `devOptional` to `dev` (`@parcel/watcher` and its platform binaries, `detect-libc`, `is-glob`, `is-extglob`).

This looks like incidental churn from a local `npm install` rather than a deliberate dependency change. Reverting `package-lock.json` keeps the PR scoped and avoids an unexplained change to production/dev pruning behavior.
</details>

@bitwarden/team-ui-foundation I'm curious on your thoughts on this one. I didn't include the loading state on purpose here. The vault team doesn't need it but to fully build out the abstraction I can add it.

@bitwarden/team-ui-foundation I kept this with `bit` as a prefix to cut down any the needed changes when this moves to the component library. This could lead to confusion as it isn't officially there yet so if you'd like to remove the `bit` aspect from it, I can!

inline.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: `disabled` is no longer wired to `BaseButtonDirective`, so a disabled FAB renders with full brand styling.

<details>
<summary>Details and fix</summary>

`hostDirectives` now lists `BaseButtonDirective` with no `inputs`, and `AriaDisableDirective` / `ariaDisableElement` were dropped in 8c42d3a. Angular does not expose a host directive's inputs unless they're listed explicitly, so:

- `<button bitFab="bwi-plus" disabled>` sets the **native** `disabled` attribute only. `BaseButtonDirective.disabled()` stays `false`, `colorClassList()` is computed with `isDisabled: false`, and the button keeps `tw-bg-bg-brand` — it looks fully enabled while being unclickable.
- No `aria-disabled` is set, so the `aria-disabled:*` variants in `getButtonColorStyles` never match, and the component diverges from `bitButton` / `bitIconButton`, which both use `AriaDisableDirective` + `ariaDisableElement` specifically to avoid the native `disabled` attribute for a11y.

The PR description still states the component "Accepts a `BitwardenIcon`, an accessible `label`, and a `disabled` state", and the `Disabled` story was removed, so it's unclear whether this was intentional.

If a disabled state is in scope, restoring it is small:

```ts
hostDirectives: [
  AriaDisableDirective,
  { directive: TooltipDirective, inputs: ["tooltipPosition"] },
  { directive: BaseButtonDirective, inputs: ["disabled"] },
],
```

plus `ariaDisableElement(element, this.baseButton.disabledAttr)` in the constructor.

If it's out of scope for VFO1, updating the PR description would avoid consumers reaching for `disabled` and getting the half-wired behavior above.
</details>

## 🤖 Bitwarden Claude Code Review

**Overall Assessment:** APPROVE

Re-reviewed at `ebf711e`; no code has changed since the previous pass, so no new inline comments were added. `VaultFabComponent` mirrors the established `BitIconButtonComponent` composition (host `BaseButtonDirective` + `TooltipDirective`, `FocusableElement` provider, `setA11yTitleAndAriaLabel` in an effect), and the new `libs/components` barrel exports (`BaseButtonDirective`, `FocusableElement`) are what a vault-owned button needs. Tailwind classes (`tw-size-12`, `tw-shadow-md`, `tw-text-2xl`, `fixedWidth`) all resolve against the base theme config and are used elsewhere in the codebase.

<details>
<summary>Code Review Details</summary>

No new findings. Previously raised points that the author resolved are intentionally not reopened: omitting `disabled` forwarding to `BaseButtonDirective` (not needed for the extension add-item use case) and dropping `ButtonLikeAbstraction`/loading per UI Foundation guidance that this is a vault-owned component rather than a CL component.

#### PR Metadata Assessment

- ❓ **QUESTION**: The description still says this adds `BitFabComponent` "to the component library" with a `disabled` state; the component now ships as `VaultFabComponent` in `libs/vault` with no `disabled` input.

</details>

@nick-livefront To answer your question and also general feedback -- per the ticket, this should be a vault-owned component, not CL. This gives us the flexibility to approach this as a more specific first-pass for VFO1 without all the rigor requirements of it being a CL component and without needing our explicit involvement. If the other teams need to access it, it can go in another shared lib that vault owns for now.  UIF will pull this into the CL as a follow-up to the beta. 

So, for your specific loading question, if it's not part of the designs for its current usages in VFO1, it does not need to be implemented.

> @nick-livefront To answer your question and also general feedback -- per the ticket, this should be a vault-owned component, not CL. 

@vleague2 Ah! I totally misinterpreted that, I appreciate the feedback! I'll move this around to be under vault and scrap anything we don't need right away.
